content:
emily-cust: Hey all — seeing a nasty repro with Go SDK streaming when requests go through our nginx proxy. Client is using go-sdk v0.4.2 and we intermittently get truncated JSON in the stream (partial object, then EOF).

Example HTTP-level behavior: nginx is set with proxy_buffering off and upstream flushes are frequent. The SDK seems to assume chunk boundaries align with JSON object boundaries and we get things like: 

  partial chunk: '{\"token\":\"Hello',
  next chunk: ' world\",\"id\":1}\n'

Resulting scanner/decoder errors in our app (stack below). Repro steps and simple server attached. Any ideas?

sam-support: Thanks, emily. Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the raw client log and the Go SDK version + exact call you used? Also do you get the same behavior without nginx (direct to upstream)?

emily-cust: Logs: 
  sdk: stream start
  sdk: got chunk (len=14) '{\"token\":\"Hello'
  sdk: got chunk (len=18) ' world\",\"id\":1}
  app: json decode error: unexpected EOF

Direct to upstream = sometimes works, more often fails through nginx.

sam-support: Ok. A couple hypotheses: 1) bufio.Scanner default token size too small and split tokens cause scan buffer growth errors, 2) SDK's stream-merge logic incorrectly reconstructs boundaries when "\n" or flushes occur inside strings, 3) nginx is adding/changing chunk framing. We'll try to reproduce.

ryan-eng: +1. Also remember bufio.Scanner splits on "\n" by default; if the SDK uses it to split by newline and the JSON objects are streamed without newlines or split in the middle of a token, Decode will hit EOF. Can you share the minimal client snippet you run?

emily-cust: Client call is just the basic streaming call: 

```go
resp, err := client.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
for scanner.Scan() {
  line := scanner.Text()
  // pass line into json.Unmarshal
}
if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("scan err=%v", err) }
```

ryan-eng: There it is — Scanner.Text yields token chunks that may be partial JSON. Using Scanner to split top-level objects only works if server explicitly delimits with "\n" between JSON objects. If upstream flushes mid-object you'll get partial tokens.

marta-qa: Quick experiment: bumping the scanner buffer helps only for very large single tokens, it doesn't solve mid-token boundary splits. Workaround: use json.Decoder on a streaming io.Reader or a custom incremental parser that handles partial reads.

sam-support: Agreed. Two immediate mitigations: 
- Change client to use json.Decoder and call Decode repeatedly (it will block until it has a full object). Example:

```go
dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)
for {
  var obj map[string]any
  if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err != nil {
    if err == io.EOF { break }
    log.Printf("decode err=%v", err)
    break
  }
  // handle obj
}
```

- If sticking with Scanner, ensure server emits a newline delimiter after each JSON object ("\n") and the SDK scanning mode is set to split on that delimiter.

emily-cust: Thanks. We tried json.Decoder and it behaves better but still occasionally returns EOF mid-decode when nginx is configured with "proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;" Any nginx config that would cause mid-object EOF?

ryan-eng: In theory no — chunked encoding shouldn't truncate objects. But some nginx settings (proxy_buffering, proxy_busy_buffers_size, fastcgi_finish_request hacks, or downstream client_disconnect) can cause upstream to think client dropped connection and close early. Can you try enabling keepalive to upstream and disabling any custom response filters? Also capture tcpdump to confirm server kept sending bytes.

emily-cust: We captured tcpdump. Upstream keeps sending the bytes — nginx forwards them, but the client (our Go app) sometimes sees EOF right after a flush boundary. Logs show Read returned 0, EOF.

sam-support: That points to client-side read semantics combined with how the SDK wraps resp.Body. Which transport are you using (default http.Client with Transport)? Any middleware?

emily-cust: Default http.Client with a custom RoundTripper that adds tracing. We removed the roundtripper and still repro. Also tested with a minimal curl -N and it prints complete objects fine.

ryan-eng: Ok. We dug into the SDK code — in v0.4.2 the stream reader has a small optimization that tries to reframe chunk boundaries by reading into a small buffer and then constructing lines for the Scanner. That code assumes boundaries won't split UTF-8 or JSON escape sequences. Edge case: if a flush splits inside an escape (like a backslash) the assembler can drop the backslash and produce invalid JSON -> decode EOF. We're going to open a PR to remove the assumption and switch to io.TeeReader -> json.Decoder pattern.

marta-qa: For immediate workaround, you can set the environment variable REDWOOD_GO_SDK_STREAM_MODE=decoder to force the SDK to use json.Decoder instead of Scanner. That env var is available in v0.4.3 patch we just cut; applying the patch in-house should fix most cases.

emily-cust: Nice — can you share the patch or a quick patch command? We can't easily upgrade the whole service yet.

ryan-eng: Paste of minimal change to client stream.go (high level):

```diff
- scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
- for scanner.Scan() { handle(scanner.Text()) }
+ dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)
+ for { var obj map[string]any; if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err != nil { if err==io.EOF { break } log.Printf("dec err=%v", err); break } handle(obj) }
```

We also added a guard to fallback to a buffered reader that stitches chunks when decoder fails briefly. Full patch PR: https://git.redwood/repro/patch/stream-decode-robust (internal link).

sam-support: We've also reproduced this locally with a tiny server that intentionally flushes mid-string. Repro server (very small):

```go
http.HandleFunc("/s", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request){
  fl := w.(http.Flusher)
  chunks := []string{"{\"token\":\"Hel", "lo\"}"}
  for _, c := range chunks { fmt.Fprint(w, c); fl.Flush(); time.Sleep(10*time.Millisecond) }
})
```

Run client with Scanner and you'll see partial tokens. With Decoder it works.

emily-cust: We applied the patch (manual change) and observed no truncation after ~2000 requests. Thanks. Any ETA on official release?

ryan-eng: We'll merge the PR after a couple more tests and cut v0.4.3 within 48 hours. If you want the hotfix backported to v0.4.2 branch let me know and I can provide a cherry-pick.

marta-qa: Followups: QA will add a fuzz test that simulates chunk splits at random byte offsets to catch regressions.

sam-support: Closing loop for now — emily, please re-open if you see recurrence after upgrade. Also filing an internal KB: "Go SDK streaming: avoid bufio.Scanner for JSON stream unless server emits explicit newline delimiters" :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #4521 updated: status -> engineering-investigating (linked PR 789).

emily-cust: Thanks everyone, that workaround and the patch worked. Very appreciated!
